pr_comments: Closing this until we decide on a more holistic approach to this issue.

issue_context.title: handle img tags in pr/issue view
issue_context.body: `` tags are dropped when rendering issue/pr markdown in the terminal. They should be rendered in the same way as other images. This is a tricky problem: - fixing it within `gh` requires regexing/parsing HTML on our own which is a brittle solution - glamour doesn't want to fix it upstream but dropping `` tags without a trace isn't an option for us. Solving this issue might mean using goldmark directly and doing a spike on what that would give us / lose for us is appropriate.
comments: The switch to glamour added rendering but still doesn't render `` tags. will update the description.

@vilmibm @ampinsk I tried solving this. Issues and PRs look like the following respectively. Does it look okay or can it be better from a design perspective? ## Issues: ## PRs: Do you want to take a look at the PR which fixes this?

@mislav I went ahead and tried fixing this because I was bored https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/3640. Would love some feedback :)

review_comments: Instead of the text `Image` there should be the alt text parsed from the `` tag. If the alt text was blank, then this text should be blank as well (`![](SRC)`). This is important for accessibility. A hardcoded alt text that just says `Image` hurts accessibility because it is not useful.
Lets avoid splitting the content into a slice of lines just to join it all together again. We can do regexp replacement on content without that.

This part is getting tricky because you're basically doing HTML parsing without writing a full-fledged HTML parser. Note that attribute values such as `src=VALUE` don't necessarily have to be closed in quotes. Furthermore, images can have text in the `alt` attribute, which would be important to parse out and preserve. Finally, an `` tag can be surrounded by regular content (like `hello world!`), so we can't just assume that an `` tag will always be on its own line and that the rest of the content can be discarded. Let's only replace the `` portion within the original content with the `![](...)` syntax and preserve everything else.

Additionally this doesn't handle image tags in code blocks which was the issue with our initial emoji rendering solution. Overall, I think we should be adding this feature into the upstream `glamour` library instead of here. @mislav what do you think?
Oh yeah 🤦 excellent point @samcoe. I do agree that this should be handled at the level that parses Markdown (so, in Glamour) rather than with regexp matching.

It sounds like the glamour team is uninterested in handling HTML: https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/issues/111#issuecomment-811291959

If that is the case, we may want to consider an alternative to glamour in the long run.

I'm going to mark this PR as a draft so we can continue discussion.
